walkthrough:
Locate Vessel X on the Diagram**
Vessel X is on the left side of the diagram, which is the right side of the heart. It opens directly into the upper chamber, the right atrium. That tells you it is a vessel bringing blood into the heart, so it must be a vein.

Link Chamber to Function**
The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood returning from the body tissues. The large veins that do this job are the superior vena cava from the head and arms and the inferior vena cava from the lower body. Either name is accepted for X here.
Final answer: vena cava (superior or inferior vena cava)

hints: Start by comparing the shading in Fig. 6.1 - which ventricle has the much thicker grey muscle wall, and where does blood from each ventricle go next?
Think about the journey each lot of blood must make - one goes only a short distance to the nearby lungs, the other goes to the whole body. What does that mean for pressure and resistance?
Link higher pressure to muscle work - why would a pump that must generate higher pressure need a thicker layer of contractile muscle, and why would high pressure be harmful in the lungs?
walkthrough:
State the Different Destinations**
The left ventricle pumps blood out in the aorta to the whole body, a long circulation with many vessels. The right ventricle pumps blood out in the pulmonary artery only a short distance to the lungs. That difference in distance is the key starting point.

Explain Pressure and Resistance**
Pushing blood around the entire body means overcoming much greater total resistance than pushing blood to the nearby lungs. So the left side must generate much higher blood pressure. High pressure in the delicate pulmonary capillaries would damage them, so right-side pressure stays low.

Link Pressure to Muscle Thickness**
Pressure is generated by contraction of cardiac muscle in the ventricle wall. More muscle means a more forceful contraction and higher pressure. That is why the left ventricle has a much thicker muscular wall than the right ventricle - structure fits function.

Final answer: Left ventricle wall is thicker than right; left ventricle pumps blood to the body (systemic circulation) over a greater distance, right ventricle pumps to the lungs; higher pressure needed to overcome greater resistance of body circulation; thicker muscle provides greater force of contraction.

hints: Think about where the heartbeat starts - a tiny patch of specialised muscle in the wall of the right atrium that fires off regular waves of excitation to the atria first.
walkthrough:
Recall the Pacemaker**
The cardiac cycle is myogenic, initiated inside the heart itself. A small region of specialised muscle cells in the wall of the right atrium spontaneously generates a wave of excitation.

Name the Structure**
That region is the sinoatrial node, often called the SAN. It sets the rhythm by stimulating the atria to contract first, before the signal passes on to the ventricles.
